data.title: Foscarnet
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antivirals & ART_

**Class:** Pyrophosphate (phosphonoformic acid) analogue

## Mechanism of action
- Directly blocks the pyrophosphate-binding site of viral DNA polymerase — does not need activation by viral thymidine kinase
- So it works against acyclovir-resistant (TK-deficient) HSV and VZV and ganciclovir-resistant CMV

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acyclovir-resistant mucocutaneous HSV and VZV in immunocompromised patients (HIV, transplant)
- Ganciclovir-resistant CMV

## Dose & formulations
- 40 mg/kg IV every 8 h (or 60 mg/kg every 12 h) for HSV/VZV; with pre-hydration; adjust to creatinine clearance

## Adverse effects
- Nephrotoxicity (acute tubular necrosis, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus)
- Electrolyte disturbances: hypocalcaemia (ionised — chelation), hypomagnesaemia, hypokalaemia, hypo/hyperphosphataemia → paraesthesia, seizures, arrhythmia
- Painful genital (penile/vulval) ulcers from high drug concentration in urine — good hygiene after voiding
- Anaemia, nausea

## Contraindications
- Severe renal impairment (relative); hypersensitivity

## Drug interactions
- Other nephrotoxic drugs; pentamidine IV (severe hypocalcaemia); QT drugs

## Monitoring
- Creatinine, Ca²⁺ (ionised), Mg²⁺, K⁺, PO₄ 2–3 times weekly; ECG

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid unless life-threatening.

## Viva points
- TK-independent — used for acyclovir-resistant HSV
- Genital ulceration from urinary excretion
- Electrolyte chaos — especially low ionised calcium

_Sources: Khopkar ch.3 (Foscarnet); Wolverton 4e ch.11. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
